title: TypeScript SDK: concurrent-consume patterns, backpressure semantics, and stress tests
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement and validate robust patterns for concurrent consumption of SDK streaming responses in Node and browser runtimes. Goals: define safe semantics for multiple consumers (dual/triage usage), formalize backpressure behavior when bridging AsyncIterable <-> Web Streams, document ergonomic helper APIs and runtime polyfill guidance, and run stress tests to quantify memory/throughput trade-offs.
work_items: Prototype DualConsumerAdapter: non-destructive tee with optional replay buffer
Define backpressure SLA: variants = immediate-drop | throttle-to-low-watermark | buffer-until-limit
Add runtime detection for native Web Streams vs polyfilled runtime and adjust TTL for buffer
Create examples: browser streaming chat with live preview + deferred final consumer
Run stress harness: 1k parallel streams, variable token rates, measure p99 latency and memory
Ship minimal ergonomic helpers: stream.share(), stream.tap(), stream.toWebStream() APIs
progress_updates: 2026-02-21: Spike completed - created DualConsumerAdapter prototype using TransformStream tee pattern for browser and a memory-backed ring buffer for Node AsyncIterable consumers.

2026-02-25: Decided against full in-memory copy for every consumer (too expensive). Chosen approach: shared underlying source with small replay buffer (configurable 'replayCount') and single-writer ordering guarantees.

2026-02-28: Implemented backpressure modes in PR 6723. Modes: 'auto-throttle' (default), 'buffer-only' (bounded buffer) and 'drop-oldest'. Trade-off note: 'auto-throttle' requires cooperative consumer yields; documented for SDK consumers.

2026-03-02: Stress test harness v1 run: 500 concurrent streams x 2 consumers, median extra memory ~2.8MB per stream, p99 latency increase ~9%. Outcome: replayCount 3 gives good UX with limited memory growth.

2026-03-04: Review feedback from PM (Sofia Patel): add browser examples that show progressive hydration for chat UIs and include guidance for server-side rendered apps to avoid double-consumption leaks.
2026-03-06: Design feedback (Amit Rao): prefer explicit 'stream.share()' helper over implicit teeing. We agreed to expose both low-level primitives and a recommended high-level API.
2026-03-08: Security review requested by release lead. Flagging potential sensitive-content retention in replay buffer - plan to wire KMS encryption for Private deployments as follow-up.
2026-03-10: PR 6723 updated with fixes: better cancellation propagation, added tests for consumer ordering, and Node ABI changes to avoid unbounded setImmediate loops. Running CI suite now.
Next: finalize docs, land PR, add a follow-up ticket for KMS-based replay buffer encryption for Private customers.
notes_on_tradeoffs: Memory vs latency: small bounded replay buffer (replayCount=3) chosen to balance immediate UX for late consumers without excessive memory growth.
API ergonomics vs explicitness: exposing stream.share() makes common cases simple while keeping lower-level converters for power users.
Runtime differences: Browser Web Streams can use TransformStream. Node relies on AsyncIterator adapters; we add a lightweight ring buffer for parity but document polyfill caveats.
Security: replay buffer holds partial response fragments temporarily; for regulated customers we must provide configurable TTL and optional encryption (follow-up work).
qa_and_benchmarks: Baseline: single consumer streaming to AsyncIterable - memory 12MB, p99 latency 120ms
Dual-consume stress test (500 streams): memory per stream +2.8MB, p99 latency +9%
High-concurrency (1k streams, replayCount=5): observed OOM on lower-memory CI runners; added guard to reduce replayCount under memory pressure
Throughput tests: transform-based tee adds ~5% CPU overhead on Node on small token payloads; acceptable for default workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Provide stream.share() helper with configurable replayCount and backpressure mode
Clear docs / examples for browser and Node showing correct cancellation and ordering semantics
Unit tests covering consumer ordering, cancellation propagation, and buffer boundaries
Stress harness results showing no OOM for 500 concurrent streams on our standard CI machine
PR merged and smoke-tested in canary runtime for one week
